chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Tadbir (manumission of a slave), so he said: 'It is in the position of a will/testament; the master may revert [to keeping the slave] in whatever he wishes from it.'

key_terms.التَّدْبِير: Manumission of a slave upon the master's death, a form of conditional freedom.
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّة: Will or testament; the legal instrument governing the distribution of estate or specific bequests.
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: To revert or revoke; the right to undo the manumission or keep the slave.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling of Tadbir in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that *Al-Tadbir* (conditional manumission upon death) holds the legal status of a will (*Wasiyyah*), granting the master the discretion to revoke it or retain the slave during their lifetime. This ruling underscores the flexibility of ownership rights in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing *Tadbir* from immediate emancipation while ensuring the slave's eventual freedom unless the master chooses otherwise. The hadith highlights the practical application of prophetic traditions regarding the merit of freeing slaves, balanced with the master's prerogative.
